findings.issue: U25 was never written, so nothing tests the editor side of the feature: the changeArrowheadSize action and panel control (testIds arrowheadSize-*), the arrowheadSize predicate (arrow tool, arrow, line with or without heads), currentItemArrowheadSize creation paths, paste styles, undo/redo, flip, restoreElements keep/drop, restoreAppState validation, and SVG export. Together these cover AC-1, AC-4, AC-5, AC-6 and FR-8 to FR-18. The changed lines in actionProperties.tsx, shapeActionPredicates.ts, actionStyles.ts, restore.ts and App.tsx have no assertions at all. The only coverage is indirect, from the regenerated appState snapshots.
findings.fix: Create the file with the 10 tests listed under U25 in change_plan.md. Render <Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally />, build elements with API.createElement/setElements/setSelectedElements, click controls with fireEvent on queryByTestId, use restoreElements/restoreAppState from ../data/restore and exportScene({type:'svg'}) from ../scene/export. Include the 'no arrowheadSize key when currentItemArrowheadSize is null' and 'no-field arrow equals today's restore output' assertions.

findings.issue: Only the default branch (triangle) of the new ~170-line getLinearElementRotatedBoundsWithHeads helper in bounds.ts is tested. No test runs the cardinality_one_or_many, cardinality_exactly_one, cardinality_zero_or_one and cardinality_zero_or_many decompositions, the circle/circle_outline radius path, the cardinality_one bar-only index-2 path, a start head, or a rotated arrow (the transformXY path). If any part offset or flag is wrong, the large-head bounds will be wrong and nothing will catch it.
findings.fix: Add one parametrised 'large heads widen bounds' case per head type (circle, circle_outline, cardinality_one, the four composite cardinality markers, and a start head). Each should assert the bounds contain every drawn part's points (for circles, center ± diameter*scale/2). Also add one case with angle != 0 that checks containment against the rotated head points.

findings.issue: This breaks the plan's test conventions: describe/expect/it are imported from 'vitest' although they are globals here, and '@excalidraw/common' is imported in two separate statements (lines 2 and 3-7). It also duplicates code: createStraightArrow is defined twice (in 'head points geometry' and in 'element bounds and hit testing'), and 'no field and medium give today's head points' repeats three near-identical API.createElement literals.
findings.fix: Drop the vitest import and merge the two @excalidraw/common imports into one. Hoist a single createStraightArrow(arrowheadSize?, endArrowhead = 'triangle', points?) helper to the top-level describe and reuse it everywhere.

findings.issue: The line case in 'small, medium and lines keep today's bounds' uses a line with no heads. The guarantee under test is that lines never widen bounds because shape.ts draws no heads for them, but the test never checks this for a line that actually has a head. The getElementBounds guard (isArrowElement) is therefore only weakly exercised.
findings.fix: Create the large line with newLinearElement plus newElementWith(line, { endArrowhead: 'arrow', arrowheadSize: 'large' }), or extend API.createElement to accept arrowheads for lines. Then assert its bounds equal those of the same line without the size.

findings.issue: In getLinearElementRotatedBoundsWithHeads, extendWithPoints takes three positional flags (isCircle, diameterScale, isCardinalityOne). As a result, call sites like `extendWithPoints(getArrowheadPoints(...), false, 1, true)` repeat about 8 times and are hard to check against shape.ts's part list.
findings.fix: Map each arrowhead to a list of parts ({ type, offset?, kind: 'circle' | 'bar' | 'points', diameterScale? }) and loop over it once, so each composite marker is a single line that mirrors shape.ts.

findings.issue: newLinearElement and newArrowElement write any truthy opts.arrowheadSize. Skeleton input from JS consumers (convertToExcalidrawElements spreads ...element) can therefore store an invalid value such as 'huge' on a new element. It renders at scale 1, but persists until the next restore.
findings.fix: Gate the spread with isArrowheadSize(opts.arrowheadSize) from @excalidraw/common instead of a truthiness check, in all three places.

findings.issue: The entry says 'Elements carry an optional arrowheadSize field'. The field exists only on linear elements (arrows and lines), so the wording overstates the public API change.
findings.fix: Change the first bullet to 'Linear elements (arrows and lines) carry an optional `arrowheadSize` field ...'.
